meta.schema: story-mode wars v1: war_id, name_en, battle_ids (chronological), located_battle_ids, camera_bbox [w,s,e,n] deg (padding 0.75), caption (EN, from sourced statement in data), caption_cites (registry ids), caption_basis, status [OK|NEEDS_CITE|NO_BATTLES]; status adds FALLBACK_ERA_BBOX (bbox = data/eras/<era>.json focus_view.bbox, bbox_source era_main_area:<era_id>) and CAPTION_PENDING_ANALYST (caption null, caption_hidden true, text kept in caption_draft)
meta.rules: Post-2023 = REPORTED, UN/OCHA/ACLED/WFP/PoE only, no control claims; contested areas drawn as contested; Arabic, if added, tagged [يحتاج تحقق].
meta.beats_schema: beats[]: {date, place_id (db/cities.json), text, source_id (registry), page, quote, badge}; from Historian /workspace/story_beats/wars_beats.json. Story threshold = battles + beats >= 2 (web/map.js swFor currently counts battles only: Web Lead to update).

wars.caption: Thutmose I's campaign against Kerma: Egyptian victory; the kingdom of Kerma was defeated.

beats.text: Tuthmose I conquered the northern Sudan, ending the independence of Kush.
beats.quote: it was Tuthmose I ( — 1530 to —1520) who accomplished the conquest of the northern Sudan; thus bringing the independence of the kingdom of Kush to an end.

beats.text: Petronius, prefect of Roman Egypt, captured Napata; Rome garrisoned Primis (Qasr Ibrim).
beats.quote: the prefect of Roman Egypt, Petronius, mounted a punitive expedition and captured Napata in —23. A permanent garrison was established by the Romans at Primis (Qasr Ibrim), which held off the Meroites.

wars.caption: An expedition from Egypt reached Dongola in 651–652; fierce Nubian resistance forced a truce.
wars.caption_basis: db/wars.json arab-nubian-wars (dongola-642 deleted by IM ruling; war starts 651, GHA III)

beats.text: An expedition from Egypt reached Dongola; fierce Nubian resistance forced a truce.
beats.quote: The Muslims from Egypt tried in 31/651-2 to conquer Nubia and even penetrated as far as Dongola but the fierce resistance of the Nubians forced them to seek a truce.

beats.text: 'Abd Allah b. Sa'd's expedition got as far as Dongola; the Christian population fiercely resisted.
beats.quote: In 31/652 'Abd Allah launched an expedition against Nubia, in present-day Sudan, and got as far as Dongola, upstream from the Third Cataract. The Christian population, close to the Monophysitic Church of Egypt, put up a fierce resistance.

beats.text: At Arbaji the Funj defeated the 'Abdallab, whose king became a vassal.
beats.quote: At Arbadji, in 1504, the Fundj defeated the 'Abdallabi and their king was reduced to the position of vassal.

wars.caption: Battle of Shaykan: Mahdist victory, a turning point of the Mahdist revolution.
wars.unlocated_note: Battles with precision=region have no lat/lon in data and are excluded from bbox; no coordinates invented.

beats.text: Shaykan, near al-'Obeid: the Ansar annihilated the Hicks expedition.
beats.quote: Another turning-point in the history of the Mahdist revolution was the battle at Shaykān on 5 November 1883. … The Ansār completely annihilated their enemy at Shaykān's forest in the neighbourhood of al-'Obeid.

beats.text: Mahdist forces took Khartoum and killed Gordon, ending Turco-Egyptian rule.
beats.quote: attacked the town, killed Gordon on 26 January 1885, and put an end to Turco-Egyptian rule in the Sudan.

beats.text: The Mahdist eastern advance was checked; the Ansar lost Tokar in 1891.
beats.quote: The Mahdists' advance on the eastern front was also checked and the Ansār lost Tokar and Kassala respectively in 1891 and 1894.

wars.caption: Battle of Gallabat (Matamma): the Emperor was mortally wounded and his army dispersed.

beats.text: At Matamma (Gallabat) the Emperor was mortally wounded; his army disintegrated.
beats.quote: The emperor hastened to Matamma to resist them, but at the close of a victorious battle on 10 March 1889, was mortally wounded by a stray bullet. News of his death caused his army to disintegrate.

beats.text: Battle of Atbara: Emir Mahmud Ahmad's Ansar failed to repel the attack.
beats.quote: Commanded by Emir Maḥmūd Aḥmad, the Ansār tried unsuccessfully to repel the enemy attack at the battle of Atbara on 8 April 1898.

beats.text: Karari, near Omdurman: the Sudanese were defeated by superior armaments.
beats.quote: the Khalīfa decided to meet the enemy in the vicinity of his capital, Omdurman … the Sudanese fought the enemy with magnificent courage at the battle of Karari on 2 September 1898. Once again they were defeated by superior armaments.

wars.caption: Sultan Ali Dinar defeated and killed; Darfur incorporated into Sudan.
wars.unlocated_note: Battles with precision=region have no lat/lon in data and are excluded from bbox; no coordinates invented.

wars.caption: The Torit mutiny of the Equatoria Corps, August 1955, is the start point of the first civil war.

beats.text: The Equatoria Corps revolted; the mutineers surrendered but disorder spread through the south.
beats.quote: in August 1955 the Equatoria Corps of the Sudanese army revolted against the gradual take-over of the administration and command posts by the northerners. Although the mutineers soon surrendered, disorder had by that time spread through the southern provinces

beats.text: Government advance from Malakal captured Bor (per HRW).
beats.quote: The second was an advance south from Malakal to capture Bor on the White Nile on April 4.

beats.text: SPLA-Torit besieged Juba and made two incursions into the town (per HRW).
beats.quote: The SPLA-Torit kept Juba under heavy siege and made two serious incursions into Juba proper in June and July 1992,

beats.text: Government forces took Torit, SPLA-Torit headquarters (per HRW).
beats.quote: They took that outpost in mid-April and Lirya in mid-May, Kapoeta on May 28 and Torit, until then the headquarters of the SPLA-Torit, on July 13.

wars.caption: Early SLA demands: regional development, an end to tribal militias, and power-sharing.

beats.text: SLA surprise attack on El Fasher damaged aircraft and looted depots (per HRW).
beats.quote: In April 2003, the SLA launched a surprise attack on El Fashir, the capital of North Darfur, and damaged several government Antonov aircraft and helicopters and looted fuel and arms depots.

beats.text: The Security Council condemned JEM's 10 May attacks in Omdurman.
beats.quote: The Security Council strongly condemns the attacks of 10 May perpetrated by the Justice and Equality Movement (JEM) against the Sudanese Government in Omdurman

wars.caption: An internal power struggle within the SPLM; fighting began in Juba on 15 Dec 2013.

beats.text: An SPLM power struggle turned to fighting in Juba's military barracks (per UNMISS).
beats.quote: The Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) became involved in the dispute, with fighting in military barracks in the capital, Juba, on the evening of 15 December, initially among the Presidential Guards.

beats.text: Defecting SPLA 8th Division forces took Bor (per UNMISS).
beats.quote: The SPLA 8th Division defected in large numbers, and took the Jonglei State capital of Bor on 18 December

beats.text: Malakal taken by defecting SPLA 7th Division soldiers and the White Army (per UNMISS).
beats.quote: The Unity State capital of Malakal was taken by defecting soldiers of the SPLA 7th Division and the White Army on 25 December.

beats.text: The SPLA division in Unity State defected and claimed Bentiu (per UNMISS).
beats.quote: the SPLA Division in Unity State similarly defected and claimed control of the state capital of Bentiu on 21 December.

beats.text: Peye's Victory Stele at Napata records his campaign against the Libyan princes of Middle Egypt and the Delta.
beats.quote: one of the inscriptions which he caused to be carved at Napata, … known as the Stele of Victory, … describing the deliberations of the king in his palace and the phases of his campaign against the Libyan princes who were masters of Middle Egypt and the Delta.

beats.text: At Hermopolis Peye found the horses dead in the stables, but forgave.
beats.quote: a great lover of horses, he is angered, at Hermopolis, to find all the horses dead in the stables but he forgives.

beats.text: Baybars's punitive expedition defeated Dawud and put Shakanda on the Mukurra throne under tribute.
beats.quote: In 1276 Baybars sent a large punitive expedition, which defeated Dāwūd, and conferred the throne of Mukurra upon Dāwūd's cousin and rival, whose name is given as Shakanda or Mashkad in the sources.

wars.caption: The Ottoman province of Berberistan, with garrisons at Ibrim, Aswan and Say.

beats.text: Özdemir Pasha re-occupied Ibrim, Aswan and Say with Bosnian garrisons; Berberistan province created.
beats.quote: in the middle of the century, Ottoman supremacy there had to be re-established through an expedition, led by the former vice-regent of Yemen, Özdemir Pasha, who re-occupied Ibrim, Aswan and Say, garrisoning them with Bosnian troops. A new province called Berberistan was established
